title: ‘This Summer Will Be Different’ Netflix Series Casts Malin Akerman, Megan Follows, Nadine Bhabha, Matias Lucas
description:
Netflix‘s series adaptation of “This Summer Will Be Different” has added four new cast members, Variety has learned. 

	Malin Akerman (“The Hunting
body:
Netflix‘s series adaptation of “This Summer Will Be Different” has added four new cast members, Variety has learned. 

	Malin Akerman (“The Hunting Wives,” “Billions”), Megan Follows (“Buried in Barstow,” “Anne of Green Gables,”), Nadine Bhabha (“Heated Rivalry,” “Slo Pitch”), and Matias Lucas (“The Order”) have all joined the drama based on the Carley Fortune novel of the same name. 


	The quartet join series leads Sophie Nélisse, Francesca Reale, and Roby Attal as well as fellow cast members Jordan Rodrigues, Jude Wilson, Natalie Brown, James Tupper, Tom Barnett, and Celia Owen. 
	

	Akerman, who currently stars in the Netflix series “The Hunting Wives,” will play Aunt Stacy. Follows will play Cherly, with Bhabha set as Farah. Lucas will play Carter. 


	“This Summer Will Be Different” was previously filming on Prince Edward Island and is now filming in Toronto. The logline for the show describes it as “a simmering, sun-soaked romance set across multiple summers on Prince Edward Island about Lucy (Nélisse), a young woman navigating her 20s and her first real love with her best friend’s (Reale) brother (Attal), the one person she was never supposed to fall for.

	The series is being adapted for the screen by Dane Clark and Linsey Stewart, who also serve as showrunners and executive producers. Fortune is also an executive producer along with Jennifer Kawaja, Elise Cousineau, and Samantha Levine for Sphere Media. 

	This marks the latest Netflix romance series based on a book or books. Most famously, Netflix airs the hit drama “Bridgerton,” which is currently prepping its fifth season. Others include “Virgin River” and “Forever,” while the romantic drama “Ransom Canyon” was recently canceled.

schema.headline: ‘This Summer Will Be Different’ Netflix Series Casts Malin Akerman, Megan Follows, Nadine Bhabha, Matias Lucas

title: Netflix, Amazon and YouTube Form D.C. Lobbying Group Amid Backlash Over Cost of Sports on Streaming
description: As U.S. politicians on both sides of the aisle have taken aim at the growing cost and complexity for Americans to watch their favorite sports teams
body:
As U.S. politicians on both sides of the aisle have taken aim at the growing cost and complexity for Americans to watch their favorite sports teams on streaming services, three of the industry’s biggest streamers — Netflix, Amazon and YouTube — have formed a new Washington, D.C.-based lobbying group to push back.

	The Streaming Access and Choice Alliance (SACA), which was announced Monday, will “promote high-quality and high-value entertainment experiences for consumers.” The group was founded by Amazon, Netflix and YouTube and is led by TechNet, a trade group that represents major technology companies.
	

	SACA “advocates for technology-neutral policies that encourage innovation in entertainment — enabling streaming services to invest in a wide range of programming, including live sports,” the alliance said in a statement. On its newly launched website, the group says, “Streaming plays a central role in bringing sports programming to wider, more diverse audiences across the country. Streaming provides multi-game viewing options, analytics-focused feeds, creator-hosted companion shows, and more — all contributing to a high-quality and personalized experience.”


	According to SACA’s founders, the volume of sports content on major global subscription streaming services has increased by 52% since January 2024.

	“Americans want more content choices and flexibility in how and where they watch their favorite programming, including sports and other live events,” Mike Ward, senior VP of federal policy and government relations at TechNet, said in a statement. “Streaming and digital entertainment companies offer audiences better features and value for their money. The industry and its customers deserve a dedicated voice in Washington, D.C., advocating for policies that enable innovation and address the needs of today’s consumers.”
	

	The formation of the Streaming Access and Choice Alliance by Netflix, Amazon and YouTube comes as the migration of sports from broadcast TV to streaming platforms has become a hot-button political issue.

	Earlier this year, U.S. Sen. Tammy Baldwin (D-Wisc.) introduced a new bill designed to “to stop professional sports leagues from blacking out games for fans, end the complicated web of streaming services and cut costs for viewers across the country.” The bill would require leagues to provide local fans with access to all of their teams’ games in one single location (either on TV or streaming) for free. According to Baldwin’s calculations, Wisconsin sports fans currently would need to pay more than $1,500 per year to be able to watch all of the Packers, Brewers and Bucks games across multiple services.

	In June, the Republican-led House Judiciary Committee held a hearing focused on the Sports Broadcasting Act of 1961, which grants professional sports leagues like the NFL a limited exemption from federal antitrust laws to collectively sell their media rights, and released a report claiming the law was “a special-interest antitrust exemption gone awry.”

	The new Streaming Access and Choice Alliance is separate from the Streaming Innovation Alliance, which launched in 2023, that advocates “for federal and state policies that build on the strong, competitive and pro-consumer market for streaming video.” Founding members of the Streaming Innovation Alliance include Netflix, Disney, Paramount, Warner Bros. Discovery, NBCUniversal’s Peacock, the Motion Picture Association and TelevisaUnivision.

schema.headline: Netflix, Amazon and YouTube Form D.C. Lobbying Group Amid Backlash Over Cost of Sports on Streaming

title: Ziwe on YouTube as the ‘Great Equalizer’ and Her Only Interview That Went South
description:
Ziwe Fumudoh has built her career in comedy and as an interview host who can handle any guest, from political figures to drag queens.

	The podcast
body:
Ziwe Fumudoh has built her career in comedy and as an interview host who can handle any guest, from political figures to drag queens.

	The podcast star and creator screened two episodes from the upcoming season of her podcast “You’d Be an Iconic Guest” — one with comedian and actress Wanda Sykes and the other with with political commentator Hasan Piker — at the Toronto International Film Festival on Sept. 10.


	Following the screening, Variety hosted a conversation in partnership with YouTube and Fumudoh, where she discussed her platform as a YouTube creator to shape discourse and direct her own content.
	

	“I think of YouTube as this sort of great equalizer,” she said, noting how hard it is to sell, develop and produce a TV series “YouTube is one-to-one. You create it, and then it’s online. That is the best experience as someone who is artistic, as someone who wants to create art. I do believe that digital creators are the new Hollywood.”

	Ziwe’s trademark interview style is both confrontational and comedic. When asked how she balances that style, she said, “I’m a good active listener. I don’t feel the need to fill dead air, and so that is comedic because someone sitting in silence as you sort of ramble is inherently hilarious.”

	She also talked about the only interview that ever went south, with the guest ending the conversation after three questions. “Sometimes the universe has different plans for us,” she said when asked why the interview ended.

	“It’s an energy thing,” she said. “I think of this as scene work, and these are my scene partners, and so we’re really catching a vibe together. And so I go into it comedy-first. Obviously, the questions and the journalism are part of the entree, but the amuse-bouche is that we are laughing and enjoying ourselves.”
	

	“Ziwe,” a variety show on Showtime, launched in May 2021. The show ran for two seasons and was canceled following a change in network leadership. She moved the show to YouTube in 2023. When asked if she would return to traditional media, she said she appreciates the freedom to be independent.

	“I started all of this because of people like Issa Rae, people like Abbi [Jacobson] and Ilana [Glazer], like ‘High Maintenance.’ They all started on YouTube, and then they went traditional,” Ziwe said. “And then you’re also finding traditional media people like Colbert or Conan O’Brien. They’re on YouTube. I go through the cycle of life in entertainment, however it may see fit. But the only thing that’s consistent is my YouTube channel.”

	And as for a late night slot of her own, she said, “I don’t know what the future holds. I will be interviewing for the rest of my life. It’s my favorite thing to do. I love asking questions. I love being messy.”

	In a recent episode with Law Roach, stylist to stars like Zendaya, the two shared a moment that has since gone viral where they touched each other’s hair. Ziwe credits that moment to a commenter. “I really appreciate the ecosystem that I’m able to have in that space,” she said. “It’s very indie, but I feel really close to my audience, and I would not have it any other way because I’m a woman of the people.”

	Ziwe made her feature film debut this year in “One Night Only,” and she said that project won’t be her last acting appearance. “I love to do one guest star role a year,” she said. “I’m passionate about acting, so yes, you’ll see me doing more. But I write, I produce, I direct, and you see that all on YouTube, which is really exciting. I just love to create. I think it’s compulsive at this point.”

	Some of her dream guests include Stephen A. Smith, Charles Barkley or Jennifer Lawrence. “The nice thing about doing the show myself is that I can interview whoever I want,” she said.

	When her subjects cross into the political sphere, she has seen pushback. “People do get really mad at me,” she said. “That’s just something I have to just turn off my phone and ignore it.”

	Regardless of who her guest is, Ziwe digs deep. “What I like about the interviews is that I feel like it’s a marriage of audiences,” she said. “You have your own world and ecosystem, I have my own world and ecosystem, and then together the interview I hope brings out something new and interesting to my audience as well as to theirs.”
	

	“As far as the politicians, yeah, people get pissed, but I think that’s part of the satire, right?” she adds. “It can’t be safe. I’m not an edge lord. I’m not trying to rage bait, but I want to continue to push myself as an intellectual, as an artist, to create something that’s really dynamic.”

	In 2029, the Oscars will be on YouTube. Would Ziwe want to present or even host? “Anything is possible,” she said. “Honestly, the world is such a big place, and I have such a powerful mind. I would never say no. Well, actually, there are a couple things I would say no to, but that is not that is not something. Sure, that sounds fun.”

schema.headline: Ziwe on YouTube as the ‘Great Equalizer’ and Her Only Interview That Went South

title: Vimeo Doubles Short Film Grant Program Prize to $300,000 (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Vimeo is launching its second annual Short Film Grant Program, doubling last year’s prize pool to $300,000 to be split among five emerging filmmaker
body:
Vimeo is launching its second annual Short Film Grant Program, doubling last year’s prize pool to $300,000 to be split among five emerging filmmakers.

	In addition to receiving funding to create an original short film, the five selected filmmakers will also receive mentorship and resources to aid their filmmaking process and accelerate their careers.

	“So many filmmakers attribute their success to the moment when someone took a chance on their work before the rest of the world knew their name. We want to create more of those opportunities,” said Ina Pira, the head of curation at Vimeo. “With Vimeo’s Short Film Grant, we’re looking to discover the next generation of filmmakers and give them the resources, encouragement and community support they need to bring their creative vision to life.”
	

	The winners will be selected by an all-new jury consisting of filmmakers Kogonada, Josephine Deck and Pete Ohs, as well as producer Sarah Winshall and cinematographer Jomo Fray. Submissions for the Short Film Grant Program will open Sept. 21 on the Vimeo website, with winners being notified by March 15.


	In its inaugural year, the program received more than 3,100 submissions. This year’s grant is supported by Panavision, Other World Computing, AJA and ShotDeck.

	“Last year’s Short Film Grant program showed us there was a real need within the industry for programs that support emerging filmmakers with financing, equipment, mentorship and distribution,” said Matteo Danieli, the co-founder of Bending Spoons, which acquired Vimeo last year. “After the overwhelming response to our first edition (over 3,100 submissions), relaunching the grant and doubling-down on the award was a no-brainer. We hope this additional capital — plus the support of our partners and jury members — will help our grant winners achieve their greatest short film ambitions.”

schema.headline: Vimeo Doubles Short Film Grant Program Prize to $300,000 (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Salma Hayek Pinault to Make Theatrical Directorial Debut With ‘Arena,’ Co-Starring Yura Borisov and Cara Delevingne (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Oscar nominee Salma Hayek Pinault is stepping behind the camera. 

	Variety can exclusively reveal that the Oscar-nominated actor of “Frida” and Emm
body:
Oscar nominee Salma Hayek Pinault is stepping behind the camera. 

	Variety can exclusively reveal that the Oscar-nominated actor of “Frida” and Emmy-nominated actress and producer of “Ugly Betty” will make her theatrical directorial debut with “Arena,” an epic romantic adventure she also wrote. The independently financed film pairs her with Yura Borisov, who earned an Oscar nomination for his role in Sean Baker’s “Anora” and is the star of Neon’s upcoming “Artificial” from director Luca Guadagnino, alongside Cara Delevingne, who co-stars in this year’s breakout hit “Club Kid,” to round out the cast.
	

	Billed as a forbidden love story about the healing power of love and desire, “Arena” is currently shooting in Mexico across the states of Quintana Roo and Veracruz — regions Hayek Pinault describes as untouched canvases as much as backdrops.


	“’Arena’ is a forbidden love story and an intimate journey into exploring someone else while finding the ability to experience intense pleasure in the simple things we take for granted,” Hayek Pinault tells Variety. “The sensorial experience of connectivity with land and nature is enhanced through the spectacular locations of Quintana Roo and Veracruz. These regions are already incredibly cinematic, but finding undiscovered beauties to shoot in this land was a true moment of pride and triumph. I am so excited to show the world these hidden jewels that have never been seen before.”

	Hayek Pinault is producing alongside formidable names, including Oscar winner Angelina Jolie (“Girl, Interrupted”), Stacy Perskie (“Bardo, False Chronicle of a Handful of Truths”), and her longtime producing partner Jose Tamez (“Beatriz at Dinner”). 
	

	Behind the lens, she assembled notable artisans, including cinematographer Philippe Le Sourd, who shot Sofia Coppola’s “Priscilla” and Wong Kar-wai’s “The Grandmaster.”

	For Hayek Pinault, this marks an evolution in her more-than-three-decade Hollywood career. She previously helmed “The Maldonado Miracle,” which earned her a Daytime Emmy Award for outstanding directing in a children’s special. “Arena” will now position her among the growing ranks of actors reshaping their careers as authors of their own vision. Additionally, she does so on home ground, in a country that has shaped her artistry.

	Hayek Pinault is represented by CAA, Entertainment 360 and Edelstein, Laird & Sobel. Borisov is represented by United Talent Agency, Curate, Gang, Tyre, Raymond, Brown & Passman and The Lede Company. Delevingne is represented by UTA, Brillstein Entertainment Partners and Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern.

schema.headline: Salma Hayek Pinault to Make Theatrical Directorial Debut With ‘Arena,’ Co-Starring Yura Borisov and Cara Delevingne (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Creator Economy Dynamo Steven Bartlett Partners With Authentic Brands to Launch OBSN Brand Development Venture
description: Rising entrepreneur Steven Bartlett has teamed with Authentic Brands to launch OBSN, a business venture designed to support creators and facilitate
body:
Rising entrepreneur Steven Bartlett has teamed with Authentic Brands to launch OBSN, a business venture designed to support creators and facilitate the development of consumer products and services built around top creators.

	The deal calls for the partners to create a platform devoted to “providing news, analysis and live experiences for the creator economy” in addition to serving as a vehicle to help creators develop and manage a range of businesses.
	

	Bartlett is the founder of Steven.com, which bills itself as the “operating system for the creator economy.” The U.K. businessman who counts more than 5 million Instagram followers hosts the popular digital series “The Diary of a CEO,” which has helped grow Bartlett’s profile in the attention-economy sweepstakes. 


	The OBSN partnership marries Bartlett’s understanding of developing and operating creator-driven business ventures with Authentic Brands’ expertise in managing products, licensing programs and retail relationships. The partners vow to “deploy hundreds of millions of dollars in the near term into creator-led businesses that meet their criteria.”

	“The next generation of global media companies and consumer brands will be built around creators. But a global audience of millions is not yet a company, and it certainly should not be the ceiling of a creator’s potential,” said Bartlett. 



	

	



	“Steven.com understands how to build media and audiences around creators, and Authentic understands how to build and extend brands around the world. OBSN brings those capabilities together so ambitious creators can reach the full scale of their ambition. We are aiming to deploy up to $400 million in creator businesses over the coming years, OBSN is at the heart of that strategy,” Bartlett said.
	

	OBSN will help build the careers of creator clients as well as nurturing IP and business opportunities that the company opts to invest in and help run. Bartlett will detail the vision behind OBSN in a live conversation set for Sept. 14 in New York with Jamie Salter, founder and executive chairman of Authentic Brands, and Maggie Sellers Reum, founder of Hot Smart Rich.

	“Creators are redefining media and shaping the future of entertainment, with many poised to become multigenerational brands in their own right,” said Matt Maddox, president and CEO of Authentic. “We are excited to partner with Steven Bartlett and his exceptional team to launch OBSN and create a powerful new model for creators and their businesses. By combining our complementary capabilities, we will identify, invest in and scale creator-led IP —  capitalizing on a once-in-a-generation opportunity to strategically deploy hundreds of millions of dollars across the creator economy and build the brands of tomorrow.”

	(Pictured: Steven.com’s Steven Bartlett and Authentic Brands’ Jamie Salter)

schema.headline: Creator Economy Dynamo Steven Bartlett Partners With Authentic Brands to Launch OBSN Brand Development Venture

title: ‘The Nature of Invisible Things’ Director Rafaela Camelo Lines Up Luciana Paes and Sundance-Winner Camila Márdila For ‘The Favorite Daughter’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Luciana Paes (“Friendly Beast”) and Camila Márdila (“I’m Still Here”) have been cast in “The Favorite Daughter” (“A Filha Favorita”), the new film b
body:
Luciana Paes (“Friendly Beast”) and Camila Márdila (“I’m Still Here”) have been cast in “The Favorite Daughter” (“A Filha Favorita”), the new film by rising Brazilian director Rafaela Camelo. The filmmaker is gearing up to shoot the follow-up to “The Nature of Invisible Things,” which premiered to acclaim at the Berlin Film Festival in 2025 and is one of the six pre-selected films vying for a chance to represent Brazil at the Oscars. In 2023, Variety named Camelo one of Brazil’s top talents to track.
	

	“The Favorite Daughter” will star Paes and Márdila as Amélia and Luiza, two sisters reflecting on their past and their relationship. When Luiza returns home after years living in Germany, she believes the trip will be a brief family visit, but things take a turn when she and her sister Amélia find out their father has a third daughter. 


	From there onwards, the family drama turns into a road movie through the backlands of Ceará as the two women are forced to confront their own history and rebuild the bond between them. 

	“The Favorite Daughter” is co-written by Camelo and André Araújo (“Gugu’s World”). The project is a co-production between Brazil’s rising Deberton Filmes via Allan Deberton and Marcelo Pinheiro – whose “Gugu’s World” premiered in Berlin earlier this year and is also gunning for the chance to represent Brazil at the Oscars– and Germany, with Maritza Grass and Vincent Edusei producing for Carousel Film. 



	

					‘The Nature of Invisible Things’
									Courtesy of The Open Reel
	



	Paes is a renowned actress who has appeared in major Brazilian works of TV and film, including Juliana Rojas’s “Necropolis Symphony” and Anna Muylaert’s “Don’t Call Me Son.” Márdila won the World Cinema Dramatic Special Jury Award for Acting at Sundance for her breakout performance in Muylaert’s “The Second Mother,” and went on to feature in other standout films, including Carolina Markowicz’s “Charcoal” and Walter Salles’s Oscar-winning “I’m Still Here.” She has recently wrapped production on Markowicz’s “The Funeral,” one of Brazil’s standout titles for 2027. 
	

	“When Luciana and Camila’s names came up together, it immediately felt right,” Camelo tells Variety. “They share a certain tone as actresses: there’s humor and warmth, but also there’s something slightly unpredictable. That was exactly what I was looking for.”

	“‘The Favorite Daughter’ is, for me, a movie about letting go of the need to be the chosen daughter so you can finally discover who you really are when no one else is assigning seats at the table anymore,” she adds of the film. “I’m interested in how conflicts can hide in plain sight within a family, beneath trivial conversations, jokes, memories, and small awkward moments. Humor becomes a way of both relieving and postponing tension. The most important conversations often happen when we least expect them.”

	Paes tells Variety she is “very happy and excited” about the opportunity to work with Camelo and share the screen with Márdila. “It is so precious to be able to look at the relationship between these two sisters with such care and rawness.” 

	“It is in our family that we allow ourselves to confront the wounds that we hide from the world,” adds the actress. “This is where we live nakedly with our imperfections. [Camelo] treads in deep waters with the fluidity of someone who has fully embraced their humanity—and loves it. I am 100% committed to the project. I always wanted to play Camila’s older sister; she’s so talented. The time has come.” 

	Márdila notes how thrilled she is to be collaborating with Camelo again after also being featured in “The Nature of Invisible Things,” and even more so given how “moved” she feels by the story. “The relationship between these two sisters goes beyond the individual, revealing both loving and thorny sides to the relationships we nurture with our origins. I always felt like I should have been Luciana’s sister; I see myself in her an awful lot, on top of her being an actress I greatly admire.”

schema.headline: ‘The Nature of Invisible Things’ Director Rafaela Camelo Lines Up Luciana Paes and Sundance-Winner Camila Márdila For ‘The Favorite Daughter’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Heartfelt, Rare Animated Belgian Feature ‘Juul’ Headlines Studio 100 Film’s Expanding Slate at TIFF Market
description:
How far would you go to keep a love one close? 

	Belgian studio Fabrique Fantastique‘s debut animated feature “Juul” comes to TIFF Market a few day
body:
How far would you go to keep a love one close? 

	Belgian studio Fabrique Fantastique‘s debut animated feature “Juul” comes to TIFF Market a few days after Studio 100 Film announced having picked up this young adult animated drama, marking a significant expansion in the otherwise family-driven catalogue of the independent sales agency, a subsidiary of Studio 100 International.

	Set in the 1950s, “Juul” follows 17-year-old circus acrobat Juul, whose life changes forever after a tragic accident leaves her in a coma and declared brain-dead. Facing financial ruin, her magician father takes a desperate and morally complicated decision: he steals her body from the hospital and presents her as a “living puppet” to revive the failing circus. 
	

	But Juul is still conscious, trapped inside a body she no longer controls. As her anger and resistance grow, her body begins to transform into porcelain, becoming a powerful symbol of her silent rebellion and her fight to reclaim her own identity.


	“From the first time I read the script, I knew we had something very special in our hands,” recalls Tom Van Gestel, CEO of Fabrique Fantastique, who also leads “Juul” as both director and producer. “If I’m being honest, it was the first I experienced so many emotions and goosebumps while reading a story. And I’ve read (and written) my share. ‘Juul’ drew me in, and I knew we had to be on top of it from the start.” 

	The script of this rare young adult animated Belgian feature was brought to Van Gestel by An de Gruyter, refined over and over with the studio’s teams. During that process, Fabrique Fantastique alum Liesbet van Loon was also brought on board as art director on the project, to craft this stop-motion like 3D-animated feature. “This technique was a clear choice for us, because of the physicality it brings to our story. ‘Juul’ is all about flesh, and how does one turn from flesh to porcelain, visually speaking.”
	



	

					Tom Van Gestel, director-producer of ‘Juul’, CEO of Fabrique Fantastique
	



	To be able to bring this transformation to the screen, along with the character’s spiraling descent into the darkest places they could actually go, 3D felt like the more natural technique the Belgian studio could use. Van Loon, whose artisanal approach to animation relied on hand-drawn ink, paint and pencils, brought her powerful artistry to the project, crafting unique characters, strange body shapes and spinning environments.

	These spirals and movements also informed “Juul”‘s score, which Van Gestel developed with five-time Grammy Award winners Snarky Puppy. “Like a carousel, they draw you in as well, into these dark places,” adds Van Gestel. “And as we kept exploring, it all came together. Form met substance, and our story informed our technique as well. Animation can sometimes do that, and as a creator, it’s a very nice feeling.”

	Turning this promising story into a fully animated 90-minute feature has been (and still is, as the film is still deep in post-production with an estimate delivery by the end of 2026) a once-in-a-lifetime experience for the CEO-producer-director. “Doing three is not ideal,” confesses Van Gestel. “But on the other hand, I’ve always liked to be a director who actually knows where the money’s going to. Sometimes, foolish discussions emerge if production and direction are not in sync, and I think our approach helped us keep a transparent and cleverly used budget.”

	And as for his responsibilities at the studio, the CEO found (as he did for his film) smart, talented people he could trust to handle the business, and plan the next years for the ever-busy animation studio. 

	Much as Van Gestel was struck by de Gruyter’s story, Studio 100 Film’s teams fell in love early with the project. But being so apart from their usual trade, it took almost a year for Van Gestel to hear back from the sales agent. “They called me and basically said ‘look, it’s now been a year, and we’re still thinking about this movie. We can’t get it out of our head. So even though it goes beyond our catalog, we just feel that we need to do it,’ and that was it. They came on board, helped us find a German co-producer and wrap the financing, and have been supporting all the way. It’s truly a joy.” 
	

	Lorena Booth, senior manager sales & acquisitions at Studio 100 Film, shares this enthusiasm and has been eager to present the project to buyers for a long time. “For us, ‘Juul’ represents the kind of ambitious animated storytelling we are increasingly looking to bring to international audiences,” she adds. “Its remarkable visual identity, emotional depth and universal themes demonstrate the creative breadth of animation today, and we are excited to present it at TIFF, and to continue expanding our slate with distinctive, filmmaker-driven productions.”



	

					Lorena Booth, bringing ‘Juul’ to TIFF for Studio 100 Film
	



	As production wraps up with a final sprint, Van Gestel reflects on his own journey with the film. “I’m a bit of a black-or-white person,” he confides, “either things are terribly bad, or they’re super awesome. And building an animated feature, you have to trust in the process because when you look at the work-in-progress images, there’s always something to redo, to improve. But with ‘Juul’, when we hit the approved button in our projection room, I am amazed at how good every shot looks. That’s both the joy and torture of making animated movies.” 

	Van Gestel, as animators hardly ever do, doesn’t forget to thank his teams, and the artists who jumped on this passion dream project turned reality. 

	“Finally being able to share it, and to get people’s reactions (and we’ve been getting a lot), it’s truly a joy. I’m very enthusiastic to see how audiences will react, and how we will build the promotion around the world we’ve crafted.” 

	Studio 100 Film brings “Juul” to TIFF Market along with its extensive slate, but there is indeed something special about this title. And, beyond its distinct look, it’s the love that radiates from all who’ve gravitated around this film, born in the heart of Belgium.

schema.headline: Heartfelt, Rare Animated Belgian Feature ‘Juul’ Headlines Studio 100 Film’s Expanding Slate at TIFF Market

title: Screen Brasil Launches Second Edition of Film Distribution Grant Initiative
description: Distribution, by common consent, has become the weakest link in the whole of the film industry. If it weren’t for public-sector aid, it would hardly
body:
Distribution, by common consent, has become the weakest link in the whole of the film industry. If it weren’t for public-sector aid, it would hardly exist. Split right deals, replacing minimum guarantees, has eased the financial stress on distributors. Every single dollar still counts, however.

	In such a context, Screen Brasil, which closes its applications for the first of two cycles of its second funding edition on Oct. 2, offers manna from heaven. Many sales agents and distributors in Europe dream of being beneficiaries from such schemes. 
	

	In its first edition, France’s Lucky Number received $15,000 to support the sales of Gabriel Mascaro’s “The Blue Trail” to Australia and Taiwan. 


	Further recipients, announced at Cannes Marché du Film this May, were Rafaela Camelo’s “The Nature of Invisible Things,” with international sales by Italy’s The Open Reel to German-speaking countries Germany, Austria, Switzerland and Liechtenstein; and Priscilla Kellen’s animated work “Papaya,” with international sales by Belgium’s Best Friend Forever to Portugal, Germany and Mexico.  

	Lucky Number has already concluded the releases in Australia and Taiwan of “The Blue Trail.” 



	

					‘The Nature of Invisible Things’
									Courtesy of Ventana Sur
	



	The grant has been a big help for the distribution of  “The Nature of Invisible Things” according to Cosimo Santoro of The Open Reel.  

	“The German distributor that participated in the call with us, GM Films, will release the film in theaters under the title ‘Sophia und Gloria – Ein Sommermärchen’ (‘A Summer Fairy Tale’),” Santoro told Variety. 
	

	“Following the theatrical run, distribution will extend to major platforms, including Amazon and the Neue Visionen Plus/Good!movies channel. Naturally, the fund will also be useful for promotional activities and the creation of materials. The smaller contribution allocated to The Open Reel — as the film’s salesagent — will enable us to release the film directly via VOD in Italy, covering the preparation of Italian-language materials (posters, subtitles and trailers). We are, of course, also organizing an appropriate press campaign for the launch. 

	As one of the six titles shortlisted to represent Brazil at the Oscars, its upcoming releases in the territories where it has been sold will also help maintain public interest, Santoro added. In addition to Germany, Austria, Switzerland and Italy, the film has sold in Latin America, Asia, the Balkans, Northern Europe, Eastern Europe, Australia, Spain, Portugal and the MENA region. 

	Screen Brasil was established last year by the Brazilian Tourism Board (Embratur) and the Olga Rabinovich Institute’s Projeto Paradiso support program with the aim of strengthening the international distribution of Brazilian fiction feature films. The initiative has increased the number of selected films from three to four and now features two selection cycles, the first of which is accepting applications from July 2 to Oct. 2. Two international distribution proposals will be selected in each cycle.

	The first call will accept films released between 2024 and 2026. The second call, taking place in the first half of 2027, will focus on films released between 2025 and 2027. Submissions must be made in English by the international sales agent holding the film’s commercial rights.

	Each selected film will receive $15,000 for international distribution efforts, including posters, translation and subtitling, marketing, trailers, ad purchases, and other strategies aimed at promoting and circulating the works abroad.



	

					Gabriel Mascaro’s ‘The Blue Trail’ likewise benefited from Screen Brasil support. 
									Credit: Guillermo Garza/Desvia
	



	Another new feature of the latest edition is an extended deadline for the start of international distribution. The window for screenings is now up to 12 months after selection, compared to the six months provided in the previous edition. This change offers greater flexibility for sales agents and distributors to define release strategies aligned with the schedules of different international markets, according to organizers.
	

	The initiative reinforces Embratur’s role in promoting Brazil across its multiple dimensions — touristic, cultural, economic, and symbolic — by recognizing audiovisual production as a key tool for the country’s international projection. For Projeto Paradiso, the partnership also represents a strategic investment in expanding international circulation opportunities for Brazilian cinema.

	“Screen Brasil was restructured in this second edition to increase the number of supported films and extend the deadline for executing deliverables,” said Roberto Gevaerd, Embratur’s director of management and innovation. “The goal is to provide sales agents with greater predictability and capacity to place Brazilian audiovisual products in international screening circuits, aligning cultural dissemination with Brazil’s image positioning goals abroad.”

	Rachel do Valle, program director at Projeto Paradiso, added: “The experience from the first edition showed a clear demand for a program like Screen Brasil. In this new edition, we increased the number of supported projects, introduced two selection rounds, and offered more flexibility for planning international releases. These changes make the support even more aligned with market dynamics and strengthen international exposure opportunities for Brazilian cinema. We are thrilled to continue this partnership with Embratur and expand the program’s reach.”

	Full regulations and application forms are available on Embratur’s website.

schema.headline: Screen Brasil Launches Second Edition of Film Distribution Grant Initiative

title: From Youtube to TIFF: ‘Brave Wilderness’ Host Mark Vins Debuts First Feature Film ‘Reef to Ridge’
description: With almost 22 million subscribers on his Youtube channel, “Brave Wilderness” host Mark Vins is no stranger to making and sharing outdoor content wi
body:
With almost 22 million subscribers on his Youtube channel, “Brave Wilderness” host Mark Vins is no stranger to making and sharing outdoor content with a global audience. Now, 14 years later, Vins has expanded from short form videos to debuting his first full-length documentary at the Toronto International Film Festival. 

	Vins’ end goal as a content creator was always to make a feature film — the TIFF premiere “Reef to Ridge” — and he knew years of uploading was the way to get him there, he told the YouTube Creators panel audience at TIFF. Variety hosted the conversation in partnership with YouTube. 
	

	His commitment to weekly videos helped him garner an audience and get in the necessary reps to pull together a full-length production. In this case, “Reef” is an exploration of the natural beauty and dangers of Ecuador’s Galápagos Islands. 


	“YouTube creators have just something really different to offer, and I think that is what is capturing the attention of cinema and film festivals now,” Vins said. “We know how to stretch a dollar. We know how to do a lot with a little. I have a joke that is if you give a YouTube creator five bucks and a stick of bubble gum, we’ll make something pretty cool.” 

	YouTubers also understand, per Vins, that content needs to consider where audiences are (usually in  their living rooms, a locale he’s happy to reach). This was especially true for “Reef to Ridge.”

	“Anytime we get to go on an adventure, that is the thought: ‘How do we bring this environment into the living room?’ How do we bring it to our audiences in a way that makes them feel like they’re here with us?” Vins said. 
	

	With Vins’ foray into feature films, a scripted, narrative story is not off the table. Now, he said, the plan is to capitalize on authenticity. “Our major goal with this project was to show people the Galápagos like they’d never seen it before, which is the authentic take,” Vins said. “To strip it away and to make it real and visceral.”

	Release plans for the film are expected in the coming weeks.

schema.headline: From Youtube to TIFF: ‘Brave Wilderness’ Host Mark Vins Debuts First Feature Film ‘Reef to Ridge’

title: Manson Family Killer and Top Lieutenant Bruce Davis Dead at 83
description:
Manson Family Top Lieutenant
                          Bruce Davis Dead at 83
body:
Manson Family Top Lieutenant
                          Bruce Davis Dead at 83
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 14, 2026
                            9:39 AM PDT
                                                                            
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Manson Family killer Bruce Davis -- who was considered one of Charles Manson's top lieutenants during their infamous, blood-soaked 1960s murder spree in Los Angeles -- is dead, TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Davis died at exactly 11:03 PM on September 11 at the California Medical Facility in Vacaville, where he was incarcerated ... according to sources and the Solano County Coroner's Office. A cause of death was not released.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Like Manson, Davis was not present at the notorious Tate-LaBianca murder scenes in which 7 people were killed by other members of the Manson Family, including film director Roman Polanski's pregnant wife, Sharon Tate.
      

            Debra Tate, Sharon's sister, tells TMZ ... "I always say a prayer upon their passing," referring to other Manson Family members who have died behind bars.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Debra adds, "Basically it says may they finally have clarity on the actions that they caused during their life, and may Lord have mercy on their souls."
      
    
            The cult killers, many of them women known as the "Manson girls," were led by Manson's other top lieutenant, Charles "Tex" Watson, on those two nights of pure butchery, during which they scrawled messages -- such as "Helter Skelter" and "Political Piggy" -- in the victims' blood on the walls.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Manson and his followers were all convicted of the Tate-LaBianca murders and were initially sentenced to death, but after California abolished the death penalty, their sentences were commuted to life in prison.
      
    
            Davis was convicted of the savage 1969 murders of Manson family friend Gary Hinman and stuntman Donald "Shorty" Shea. He confessed to police that he sliced Shea with a knife and was armed with a gun as Manson sliced off Hinman's ear with a sword.
      
    
            Over the years, he was repeatedly denied parole. When he was denied parole in 2022 ... Davis' attorney Michael Beckman said the parole commissioner told him he "lacks empathy."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            In January 2024, his parole hearing was postponed months after he appeared on the podcast "The Lighter Side of Serial Killers."
      
    
            He wrote to host Keith Rovere in a 2023 Christmas card that he was "looking forward" to the parole board hearing before it was moved to August 2024, before being denied ... Fox News reported.
      
    
            Davis was 83.

title: Accused Lindsay Clancy Copycat Rambled To Cops In Unhinged Interview After Alleged Murder
description:
Accused Lindsay Clancy Copycat
                          Unhinged Police Interview ...
body:
Accused Lindsay Clancy Copycat
                          Unhinged Police Interview ...
                          After Alleged Murder
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 14, 2026
                            8:59 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Corie Walsh rambled to police about McDonald's and started singing a tune from "The Wizard of Oz" after she allegedly killed her child while paying close attention to the Lindsay Clancy trial.
      
    
            Walsh, the mother of four in Illinois who is charged with murdering her son, talked to cops after her 2-year-old was found dead in the basement of their family home earlier this month ... and she told them she went to Mickey D's for a breakfast sandwich in the afternoon ... her attorney, Robert Kerr, reportedly told the judge.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            That doesn't make much sense ... McDonald's doesn't serve breakfast in the afternoon.
      
    
            What's more, Walsh's defense says she started singing "Follow The Yellow Brick Road" while talking to investigators.
      

            On her way from the death scene to a nearby hospital, Walsh's defense says she was "in and out of consciousness" and was incoherently talking to paramedics ... telling first responders they "looked like her daughter."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            During the ambulance ride, Walsh started rattling off fruit names ... her defense said.
      
    
            Prosecutors say Walsh was texting about the Clancy murder trial in a group chat on the day her son died. Authorities have not established that the Clancy case caused or directly influenced what happened.
      
    
            Walsh's defense team argues she was experiencing a psychotic episode when her son died.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Prosecutors say she told cops she killed her son because he was the devil and the antichrist ... and she allegedly plotted to poison her husband too.
      
    
            And, get this ... her defense says she told investigators she drowned her kids one by one ... but that's not even close to what actually went down. None of her kids drowned, and none were found in water. Only her 2-year-old was killed, and the other children weren't harmed.

title: Kylie Jenner Unloads Los Angeles Mansion for $15.3 Million
description:
Kylie Jenner
                          Hidden Hills Home Sells Nearly $5M Under Ask
body:
Kylie Jenner
                          Hidden Hills Home Sells Nearly $5M Under Ask
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 14, 2026
                            8:44 AM PDT
                                                                            
              
    
            Kylie Jenner just scored a $15.3 million payday ... selling her stunning Hidden Hills mansion ... for about $5 million less than the original asking price.
      
    
            The Daily Mail first reported the sale closed Friday, months after Kylie put the luxury estate on the market for $20.25 million.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Kylie originally purchased the sprawling 13,200-square-foot property for $12.05 million in late 2016.
      

            The 8-bedroom, 10-bathroom mansion sits on a private lot with sweeping city and pastoral views. It features a private theater, game room with wet bar, executive office with fireplace, gym, and massage room.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The primary suite includes a sitting area, dual oversized closets, a spa-like bathroom, and a private balcony overlooking the property.
      
    
            The home also has an attached guest suite with its own entrance, bedroom, bathroom, kitchenette, sitting area, and courtyard.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Outside, the resort-style property boasts a pool and spa, expansive patio, outdoor kitchen, fire pit lounge, circular driveway, six-car garage, and ample guest parking.
      
    
            'Million Dollar Listing' stars Josh, Matt, and Heather Altman represented the property. They had no comment on the sale.

schema.headline: Kylie Jenner Unloads Los Angeles Mansion for $15.3 Million
